result:
If I had to choose a single change, it would be to **eliminate the human capacity for dehumanization.** 

Most of the worst atrocities and systemic cruelties in history don't happen because people wake up wanting to be evil; they happen because people convince themselves that the "other"—whether defined by nation, ideology, class, race, or belief—does not feel, hurt, or matter in the same way they do. Abstraction and distance allow harm to feel justifiable, efficient, or necessary.

If every person were fundamentally incapable of reducing another human being to a label, a statistic, or an obstacle—if the reality of another person's inner life and suffering were always as vivid and undeniable as their own—most forms of warfare, exploitation, and systemic neglect would collapse under the weight of their own impossibility.
